items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: Where does 了 go in the fever sentence?
items.answer: 了 goes on the condition that has happened: 發燒了. Do not add a second 了 to the result 吃藥.

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Say what you expect will happen.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: 會 before an action can mean “will” — something you expect in the future. A time word makes the future meaning clear.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

items.question: Do I add 了 when 會 means something will happen tomorrow?
items.answer: No. 會 already marks the expected future: 我明天會來。 Do not add 了 to the future action.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do something with someone, speak to someone, or get something from someone.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: 跟 comes before a person. It can mean “with” (do something together), “to” (speak or ask a person), or “from” (learn or borrow from a person). A helping verb or adverb goes before 跟.

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: In this pattern the subject comes first, then 跟 + the person who joins you: 我跟朋友去醫院。 A different subject can lead, as in 朋友跟我去醫院, but the 跟 phrase still comes before the action.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

items.question: I speak Chinese to the doctor — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Put 跟 right before the person you speak to: 我跟醫生說中文。 The subject comes first; the 跟 phrase comes before the verb.

right.english: I speak Chinese to the doctor.

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

text.english: You should exercise more and drink a little less alcohol.

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

items.question: Do I add 了 when 會 means something will happen tomorrow?
items.answer: No. 會 already marks the expected future: 我明天會來。 Do not add 了 to the future action.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: Where does 了 go in the fever sentence?
items.answer: 了 goes on the condition that has happened: 發燒了. Do not add a second 了 to the result 吃藥.

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Choose the result signal and response.

questions.correctFeedback: 就 introduces the complete result.
The result needs an action.
就 opens the result; 多 adjusts 休息.

grammarPages.exerciseNote: The book answers three questions with 要是/如果……，就…… on printed page 237 and gives no answer key; these model answers follow the printed prompts.

text.traditional: 你覺得哪裡不舒服？
text.simplified: 你觉得哪里不舒服？
text.pinyin: Nǐ juéde nǎlǐ bù shūfu?
text.english: Where are you uncomfortable? (What brings you here today?)

text.traditional: 我咳嗽、頭痛，鼻子也不舒服。
text.simplified: 我咳嗽、头痛，鼻子也不舒服。
text.pinyin: Wǒ késou, tóu tòng, bízi yě bù shūfu.
text.english: I have a cough and headache. Also my nose is uncomfortable.

text.traditional: 最近天氣冷了，很多人感冒了。
text.simplified: 最近天气冷了，很多人感冒了。
text.pinyin: Zuìjìn tiānqì lěng le, hěn duō rén gǎnmào le.
text.english: The weather is getting cold recently, many people got colds.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish
ending word: a change or a finish

text.traditional: 對啊！聽說我們學校感冒、發燒的學生很多。
text.simplified: 对啊！听说我们学校感冒、发烧的学生很多。
text.pinyin: Duì a! Tīngshuō wǒmen xuéxiào gǎnmào, fāshāo de xuéshēng hěn duō.
text.english: Right! I heard that many students from my school have a cold and fever.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.traditional: 最近也有很多人肚子痛。
text.simplified: 最近也有很多人肚子痛。
text.pinyin: Zuìjìn yě yǒu hěn duō rén dùzi tòng.
text.english: Many people have a stomachache as well.

text.traditional: 是因為吃的東西不乾淨嗎？
text.simplified: 是因为吃的东西不干净吗？
text.pinyin: Shì yīnwèi chī de dōngxi bù gānjìng ma?
text.english: Is it because of having contaminated food?

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.traditional: 不是，這也是因為感冒。
text.simplified: 不是，这也是因为感冒。
text.pinyin: Bú shì, zhè yě shì yīnwèi gǎnmào.
text.english: No, it is also due to having a cold.

text.traditional: 請問我需要吃藥嗎？
text.simplified: 请问我需要吃药吗？
text.pinyin: Qǐngwèn wǒ xūyào chī yào ma?
text.english: Do I have to take any medicine?

text.traditional: 我會給你三天的藥。你要記得多喝一點兒水，要是發燒了，就吃紅色的藥。
text.simplified: 我会给你三天的药。你要记得多喝一点儿水，要是发烧了，就吃红色的药。
text.pinyin: Wǒ huì gěi nǐ sān tiān de yào. Nǐ yào jìde duō hē yìdiǎnr shuǐ, yàoshi fāshāo le, jiù chī hóngsè de yào.
text.english: I will give you medicine for 3 days. Remember to drink plenty of water. If you have a fever, then take the red pill.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

text.traditional: 好，謝謝醫生。
text.simplified: 好，谢谢医生。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, xièxie yīshēng.
text.english: Okay, Thank you doctor.
